lead: One or two plain sentences stating the outcome up front. Leave empty to omit this section.

beats.title: Short plain-language headline for this step
beats.desc: 2–4 plain sentences. No jargon, no arrows, no memo codes in the prose. Explain it to a smart non-expert.

whys.problem: One sentence naming the failure to be explained.
chain: The answer is now a fixable cause, not another symptom.
whys.root: One or two sentences stating the true root cause the chain arrived at.
fixes: A concrete change that would prevent recurrence.

_help.cls_meaning: start=run begins; credential=key/secret event; kill=stopped for good; block=blocked/failed; memo=decision; progress=passed a gate; launch=started work; heartbeat=routine check; other=everything else
_help.whys_count: Do 5–7 whys per chain. One chain per distinct root failure (usually 1–3 chains).
_help.style: ISO house style: short sentences, plain words, active voice, neutral tone, no insider jargon.
_help.ground_truth: Check every claim against telemetry, not just the log. Any quantity you state in a beat or why (tool counts, subagent counts, retries, message timing) must be countable from .telemetry.jsonl. Only message.in records have a wall-clock timestamp; tool events are ordered but not timestamped, and durationMs exists on only some tools. Do not invent timing or counts the telemetry cannot support. The build renders the counts panel for you — mirror those numbers, don't guess.
